judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Escrow Account definition requires all Cash and receivables to be deposited there, while this requires the same categories of proceeds to go into a different account; the overlap is left to the Collateral Account Agreement to resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names a firm and permits reputable substitutes; definite enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-refers to Sections 4.01(j) and 5.07(b) and fits the Consultants definition. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Narrow and specific: premium financing from non-affiliate institutional providers in the ordinary course. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Presumably a Section 6.01 permitted debt basket; nothing reproduced contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditional on appointment and acceptability, but the wording is clear about role and capacity. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Agents and Intercreditor Agreement definitions, which likewise treat the role as contingent. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "In form and substance satisfactory to the Borrower and the Required Lenders" leaves the document wholly to be agreed, an agreement-to-agree flavour. Moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several definitions (Supplier Financing, Secured Party, Common Project Financing Facility) presuppose such an agreement will exist, so its absence would leave pari passu sharing unresolved; that is a latent gap rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Describing it as "the one-time request" is unusual for an interest election but is stated plainly. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.07(b) confirms the election is made once in the first Borrowing Request, so the definition matches. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed percentage; entirely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in Sections 2.06(h) and 2.13; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ties payment to the last day of the applicable Interest Period; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Interest Period definition and Section 2.13. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumeration runs "(i) ... and (iii)" with no clause (ii), a plain mechanical error in a provision that also has to make all Interest Periods concurrent. That defect is nameable and affects a mechanical rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.07(a) reproduces the identical (i)/(iii) sequence, so the two are consistent with each other even though both are defective.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but structured, with a clear valuation rule; "assets of any Person constituting a business unit" is mildly soft. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Permitted Investments, Cash Equivalent Investments and the Adjusted Tangible Net Worth deduction for advances to Affiliates. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite as to the initial Issuing Bank and the affiliate-extension mechanic. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.06(e) expressly handles the affiliate case by converting the LC Disbursement into a Term Loan of the affiliated Lender; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permits the Issuing Bank's own form subject to the Borrower's reasonable acceptance; workable and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.06(b)/(f) and Exhibit C. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, precise definition of a payment under a letter of credit. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.06(e), (g) and (h). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (b) opens "the sum of (i) ... plus the aggregate amount" without a clause (ii), an enumeration slip; the arithmetic is still recoverable. Nameable mechanical defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with Unused Commitment, Term Loan Exposure and Section 2.06(a)'s sizing test; those are consistent with the intended reading.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Refers to an assignee becoming "a Project Lender pursuant to an Assignment and Assumption", conflating the recital term "Project Lender" with "Lender". A small definitional slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Project Lender" is defined only in the recitals and includes supplier's credit providers, so using it here to describe an assignee Lender blurs the two categories relative to Section 9.04.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard fund/affiliate formulation; definite in structure. Nothing named.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The term does not appear to be used in the reproduced operative text, which is a drafting redundancy rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Like its siblings it closes with the garbled "on the same terms as the required by the Loans" and conditions the whole quotient on other creditors' requirements. Nameable defect in a payment-allocation formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is keyed to Section 2.11(b), yet the Cash Sweep Mechanism directs application of the Sweep Amount "pro rata to each Lender in accordance with its Lender's Pro Rata Interest in accordance with Section 2.11(c)(vii)" — two different prepayment provisions for the same fraction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition packs issuance deadlines, a double expiry test, and four numbered conditions into one sentence, and the closing words "issued pursuant to this Agreement and an Issuing Bank Agreement" dangle after item (4). Mechanically awkward and arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item (4) fixes the last negotiation date at 30 December 2014 while limb (ii) caps expiry at four years from 29 December 2010 — one day earlier — and Section 2.06(c) repeats only the expiry test.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pointer to the recitals; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recitals do define the Letter of Credit Facility. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The fallback sentence begins "In the event that such rate is not available at the time of determination for any other Interest Period", where "any other" has no antecedent and confuses the fallback's trigger. That is a nameable defect in a rate-setting mechanic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Market Disruption Event definition refers to the Reuters "LIBOO1" screen whereas this definition uses "LIBOR01", an inconsistency between two provisions governing the same rate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional two-limb Lien definition; broad but precise. Nothing named.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Permitted Encumbrances, Section 6.02 and the Security Documents. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixes the pledge at 51% of Equity Interests and requires a form reasonably satisfactory to named parties; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches "Pledged Borrower LLC Interests" (not less than 51%) and the 49% Change in Control threshold. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list ends with "any other document designated from time to time as a Loan Document by the Lenders or the Facility Agent", a unilateral open-ended catch-all following enumerated documents. Genuine general-vs-specific tension, and one-sidedly drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because "Obligations" and the Events of Default attach to all Loan Documents, this unilateral designation power interacts with Section 9.02's amendment restrictions; that interface is where a dispute would arise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One line, definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Term Loan and Sections 2.01–2.05. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The phrase "deferred payment guaranties, shortfall undertakings or payment undertakings or any nature whatsoever" is garbled (evidently "of any nature") and functions as an unbounded catch-all after specifics. Both defects are nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with Short-Term Debt and Total Debt, which use the same garbled formula; internally consistent even if defective.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names a single institution and capacity; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the preamble. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Each limb is keyed to the Required Lenders' own determination, with no objective standard or good-faith qualifier, and limb (iii) uses the vague "in excess of the LIBO Rate". That subjectivity is nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites the Reuters "LIBOO1" screen while the LIBO Rate definition cites "LIBOR01", and it interacts with Section 2.14's alternate rate mechanics; the screen mismatch is a specific inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Material adverse effect" is the paradigm open-textured standard, and limb (a) measures it against a fixed date ("since March 31, 2010") while limbs (b) and (c) are not so anchored. The term is squarely nameable as vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is used throughout (Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted Tangible Net Worth, Total Assets, Sections 3.04, 5.02, Article VII), and those uses are consistent with a single elastic standard rather than contradicting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All material approvals and consents by any Person" is unbounded as to materiality and is then extended by "including, but not limited to" — a general-plus-specific structure with uncertain reach. Nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to "Schedule 4.01(f)" whereas the schedule index lists "Schedule 4.02(f) Material Project Approvals", a direct mismatch between this definition and the schedules to the same instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference to the LLC Pledge Agreement; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the LLC Pledge Agreement definition. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies a dated loan agreement and its amendments precisely. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Permitted Encumbrances clause (q), which preserves the Minnesota State Loan liens on stated terms. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A named rating agency; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in Permitted Investments. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Enumerates instrument types and requires reasonable satisfaction of Lenders and Security Agent; definite enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Mortgaged Property, Security Documents and Section 5.14. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (ii) sweeps in "any and all mining rights and leases ... with acknowledgment from the relevant Government Authorities", which leaves unclear whether the acknowledgment is a condition of inclusion. That is a nameable ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on Schedule 1.01D, the Additional Collateral Date definition and Section 5.14; those fit together, though the acknowledgment condition may not match Section 5.14's absolute obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory cross-reference; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Plan, ERISA Event and Withdrawal Liability. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The arithmetic is garbled — "minus, (B) ... and (C) minus mark-to-market amounts" — and the $25,000,000 threshold qualifier's placement is unclear. A nameable mechanical defect in a covenant input.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to the "Unrestricted Account established in accordance with the Collateral Account Agreement", a term not defined in this Agreement though used again in Permitted Project Change and the Unsecured Subordinated Promoter Loans definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple subtraction of two defined terms, though "for any period and at any time" is redundant for a balance-sheet measure. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Total Assets and Total Debt. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and duplication-guarded; the components are enumerated. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Cash Sweep Net Finance Charges (narrower scope) and Debt Service. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but structured with express netting rules; "reasonably estimated to be payable ... as determined reasonably and in good faith by a Financial Officer" imports judgment but with a standard. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to "any Foreign Subsidiary" although the Subsidiary definition states the Borrower has no Subsidiary, a form leftover that produces a small incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition ends circularly ("in each case to the extent arising in connection with the Obligations"), a nameable self-reference in the term that anchors the security package.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors Additional Obligations and feeds Secured Obligations and the Security Agreement; consistent in structure across those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any of the Borrowers" is plural where the Agreement has a single defined Borrower, a form leftover. Minor mechanical slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Borrower definition and preamble identify one borrower, so the plural here is inconsistent with the rest of the instrument, albeit harmlessly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 45-day spot sale carve-out is precise, though the sentence ends without punctuation. Little substantive ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with the Project Contract definition's Consent and Agreement requirement, which expressly excepts Offtake Contracts from the threshold carve-out; the two read together coherently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Enumerated tax types closing with "or similar taxes, charges or levies", a modest catch-all in a conventional formulation. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Taxes, Excluded Taxes and Section 2.17. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pointer to the recitals; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recitals define Parent. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.04(c) is the participations provision. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory citation; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 9.15. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory body reference; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the ERISA Event definition. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "De-bottlenecking and other similar performance and operational and efficiency enhancing modifications" is a vague catch-all standard for what capex qualifies, despite the hard $50,000,000 cap. The qualitative limb is nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same phrase recurs in the Permitted Project Change definition, which uses it to switch off the Required Lenders' consent, so the scope of the phrase has consequences across two provisions; they are drafted consistently though.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing proviso reads "shall not include any Lien securing Indebtedness on Attributable Debt", where "on" appears to be a slip for "or", and the eighteen-limb list contains multiple "other similar"/"like nature" catch-alls. Both a mechanical error and general-vs-specific tension are nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The term is the gateway to Section 6.02 (Liens) and is also invoked, under the wrong name "Permitted Liens", in the FACR definition; that mismatch is a specific cross-provision problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference to Section 6.06; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Net Debt, Long-Term Debt and Short-Term Debt references to Permitted Hedging Agreements. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference to Section 6.01; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Additional Indebtedness and Net Debt. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (e) permits repurchase agreements "with a maturity not less than one (1) year thereafter", the opposite of the short-maturity logic of clauses (a)–(d) and evidently a slip for "not more than". That is a clear mechanical error changing meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Cash Equivalent Investments (twelve-month/six-month maturities) and the Net Finance Charges credit for interest on Permitted Investments; the (e) anomaly is out of line with that scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition uses "inter alia" before an illustrative list and then stacks two provisos that alternately require and dispense with Required Lender consent, leaving the consent rule genuinely arguable. Nameable general-vs-specific and internal tension.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "Project" definition incorporates Permitted Project Change subject to approval, and Permitted Capex Additional Indebtedness carves out the same modifications, so the consent question ripples across three definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list ending in "or other entity"; conventional and unproblematic. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently throughout. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Keyed to specific ERISA/Code provisions; definite despite OCR rendering "BRISA". Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with ERISA Affiliate, ERISA Event and Section 3.10. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixes a continuing 51% floor by reference to the LLC Pledge Agreement; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the LLC Pledge Agreement definition and the 49% Change in Control threshold. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The tail is grammatically broken and redundant: "subject to the receipt of approval, if any, required in the definition of Permitted Project Change has been approved as set forth in the definition of that term". A plain mechanical defect in a term that fixes the scope of the secured business.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the Permitted Project Change definition (itself proviso-laden) and on the recitals' description of the Project, so the boundary of "Project" is set by three interacting texts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition runs to a single sentence with three nested provisos, a $4,000,000 "Contract Threshold" aggregating "the same or similar products or materials", a schedule-based exception, and a further redefinition for Sections 6.09 and 6.10. Both "similar products or materials" and the layered carve-outs are genuinely arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly overrides "any other provision to the contrary in this Agreement" and alters what Sections 4.02, 5.14(i), 6.09 and 6.10 require, so its interaction with those operative sections is precisely where a construction fight would occur.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pointer to the recitals; definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recital definition of "Project Lenders" bundles term lenders and supplier's credit providers, which is broader than "Lender"; the Lender definition then uses "Project Lender" for assignees, a mild crossover.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies a specific dated contract; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Listed among the EPC Contracts. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names four banks with an appointment mechanism and a reasonableness qualifier; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in the Market Disruption Event definition; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard enumeration of affiliates and personnel; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supports Sections 9.03 and 9.12; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defers entirely to dates "specified in the financial Covenants", with lower-case "financial Covenants" not exactly matching the defined term. A minor slip with an otherwise clear meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on Section 6.12 (not reproduced) to supply the dates; if that section does not specify them, the term is empty, but nothing reproduced contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two alternative periods are given as (a) and (b) with no conjunction and no rule for which applies when, so a covenant tested "for the Relevant Period" could be tested over either. That is a nameable ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because the financial covenants in Section 6.12 are not reproduced, the choice between (a) and (b) cannot be resolved from the rest of the text, which heightens rather than cures the problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference to Section 5.15; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.06(j) also refers to the Required Amount "thereunder"; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise 51% test with a clear before/after switch between Commitment Percentages and Term Loan Exposure. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Commitment Percentage, Term Loan Exposure and Section 9.02. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of offices; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.04 permits certification by a Responsible Officer "or other officer or director reasonably acceptable to the Facility Agent", which widens but does not contradict this.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but enumerated, with an express Tax Distribution carve-out; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Tax Distributions, Synthetic Purchase Agreement and Section 6.07. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A named rating agency; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in Permitted Investments. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It provides for a mutually determined date but overrides it with a hard 30 June 2013 long-stop; the wording is definite even if the mechanism is unusual.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Cash Sweep Mechanism's First Sweep Period begins nine months after this date and ends 1 April 2014, so a 30 June 2013 date leaves that window very short — a timing strain with that definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.14 supplies the meaning. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-limb aggregation with a duplication guard; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Obligations, Additional Obligations, Secured Party and the Security Agreement. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical "(sharing pari passu in respect of the security interests of the Lenders in the Collateral, directly or through EPIL under the Supplier Financing)" is compressed and leaves the mechanism of sharing unclear. Modest nameable ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sharing depends on an Intercreditor Agreement that is only contingently required ("in form and substance satisfactory to the Borrower and the Required Lenders"), so pari passu status here rests on a document that may not exist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names Wells Fargo in an agency capacity with successors; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the preamble, Security Agreement and Article VIII. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The body promises a "first perfected security interest" in all Collateral while the proviso makes the interest in Current Assets junior to a Working Capital Bank; the two pull against each other within one sentence. That tension is nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The FACR definition assumes a "first priority security interest" over fixed assets and the Collateral definition is unqualified, so the Current Assets subordination has to be harmonised with those; it can be, but the seam is real.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list closing with "each other security agreement or other instrument or document executed and delivered pursuant to Section 4.01 and Section 5.14", which is anchored by section references rather than open-ended. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps with "Additional Security Documents" but is consistent with it and with the Collateral definition. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It repeats the garbled "payment undertakings or any nature whatsoever" formula and adds an open-ended "other obligations and liabilities maturing within one (1) year". Both a mechanical slip and a catch-all are nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors Long-Term Debt and feeds Total Debt, which are drafted in the same terms; internally consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Points to Exhibit K or another reasonably acceptable form; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Unsecured Subordinated Promoter Loans definition and Exhibit K. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two routes plus a consent proviso for non-institutional Persons; the categories ("governmental export credit agency or similar governmental finance entity") include a mild catch-all. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.20, the Accession Agreement mechanism and the Common Project Financing Facility definition. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consolidation/50% formulation; definite though lengthy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is distinguished from capitalised "Subsidiary" in the immediately following definition, a case-sensitive distinction that could be missed but is expressly drawn.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Combines a definition with a factual statement ("the Borrower has no Subsidiary"), which is a representation embedded in a definition. Mildly unusual but clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Net Proceeds definition refers to "any Foreign Subsidiary" and Section 5.12 addresses Subsidiaries, so the no-Subsidiary statement sits awkwardly against those form provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference to Section 6.03(a); definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Borrower definition's reference to permitted successors. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single long sentence combining a cap, a repayment-schedule constraint, a schedule-conformity requirement and an assignment obligation; "substantially on the same terms and provisions as are set forth in Schedule 6.01" is soft. Moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cap of US$183,000,000 sits against the Financial Closure requirement of US$182,750,000 of Supplier Financing and the Upstream Supplier Financing Creditors definition's requirement of identical terms; the near-identical figures invite argument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies a dated contract; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Listed as an EPC Contract. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies a dated contract; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Listed as an EPC Contract. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad ("any swap, derivative or other agreement or combination of agreements") but with a clear phantom-stock carve-out. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Restricted Payment definition, which expressly captures payments under a Synthetic Purchase Agreement. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Solely to the extent actually necessary" to discharge "actual tax liabilities" is a tight, quantifiable limit. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Restricted Payment carve-out and Section 6.07. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Enumerated and closed with "in the nature of a tax"; conventional and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Excluded Taxes, Other Taxes and Section 2.17. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line definition citing two sections in reverse order; harmless and definite.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixed start and end dates with an early-termination proviso; definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Letters of Credit may be issued to 30 June 2013 and can convert into Term Loans on drawing, potentially after 30 September 2013 when Section 2.01 says undrawn commitments lapse automatically — a timing strain with Sections 2.01 and 2.06(e).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Shall be set forth or in the Assignment and Assumption or Accession Agreement" contains a stray "or", a clear typographical slip that does not obscure meaning. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.08, 2.20 and 9.04 and with the Total Commitment figure. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple sum of principal and LC Exposure; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Required Lenders and LC Exposure. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pointer to the recitals; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recitals define the Term Loan Facility, including its increase on Accession Project Financing. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear either/or formulation; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Term Loan Commitment and Term Loan Exposure. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single fixed date; entirely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the final instalment date in the Section 2.09 table, though Section 2.09's "next preceding Business Day" convention would move a 1 January payment earlier; that is a mechanic, not a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: GAAP-based with a bespoke deduction for litigation-related contributions; the deduction is wordy but specified. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the same carve-out in Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted Tangible Net Worth and feeds Net Equity. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed amount with a stated increase mechanism and a hard cap; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the recitals ($250M initial, up to $530M), the Financial Closure definition and Section 2.20. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It uses "Working Capital Bank Finance" where the defined term is "Working Capital Bank Financing", and "without duplications" is a plural slip. Nameable but minor mechanical errors.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The mismatch is with the "Working Capital Bank Financing" definition (and with Indebtedness clause (i)'s "Working Capital Bank Facility"), so three provisions use three labels for one concept.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but bounded by "in connection with the Transactions"; definite enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Transactions and Section 2.02(d)'s permitted use of proceeds. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (b) — "the completion and operations of the Project and any matters related thereto" — is extremely broad for a term that governs Transaction Costs and accounting adjustments. Nameable breadth.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because Section 2.02(d) permits proceeds to be used for "Transaction Costs", the breadth of limb (b) enlarges permitted use; the provisions are consistent but the breadth carries through.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is a run-on that narrates rather than defines — "and certain of which ... are excluded from certain definitions as used herein" — and cites "Section G.07". Vague and mechanically defective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to the Unrestricted Account, which is not defined in this Agreement, and to Section 6.07's payment restriction and Section 4.04(e)'s test, so its operation depends on texts it describes only loosely.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple arithmetic definition; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.01, 2.06(a)/(b) and 2.08. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names two specific institutions and imposes identical-terms conditions; definite, though "shall be or shall become Secured Parties" is loose as to timing. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires terms identical to the Supplier Financing including principal amount, while Financial Closure speaks of US$182,750,000 and Supplier Financing of US$183,000,000; that figure gap touches this condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Like the parallel pro rata definitions, it ends in the ungrammatical "on the same terms as the required by the Loans" and makes the fraction contingent on other creditors' requirements. Nameable defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is keyed to Section 2.11(f) and matches the structure of the Lender and Additional Indebtedness pro rata definitions; consistent among themselves.
judgments.clause_name: Definition — "Upstream Supplier Financing Creditor's Pro Rata Interest"

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A 100% ownership test with a de minimis qualifying-shares exception; definite.
